children: on Thursday (beat on EPS, lower than expected sales), Molson Coors
was downgraded to Underweight from Equal Weight at Wells Fargo ahead of what is expected to be a challenging 2027. The target price was cut to $36, suggesting a further 15% downside.
Analyst Chris Carey sees several headwinds that could undermine future results, especially the brewer’s gross margin as inflation keeps the pressure on cost of goods sold.
Carey also sees increased earnings risk and valuation risk, both of which will amplify profit-taking pressure on TAP given the recent gains in tandem with the consumer sector.

“Molson Coors confronts two key headwinds that have not eased. First, the beer category typically sees volume declines, even if year-to-year trends can be better or worse, depending on a variety of factors. Second, TAP typically loses market share,” Carey writes in a note to clients, adding that the ability to grow profit will be made more difficult with any additional inflation headwinds.

Following third-quarter results, Carey sees too much downside to his EPS estimates to remain on the sidelines with an Equal Weight rating, hence a downgrade to Underweight. He now estimates 2027 EPS at $3.31 from $3.95 previously, organic sales down 1.6%, and volume down 3.3%. This compares to consensus estimates of $4.31 EPS, flat organic sales, and a -1.8% volume decline.
“Our estimates may prove too high if category softness and TAP share losses persist," Carey adds.
The downgrade, coupled with the lingering fallout from Thursday's quarterly report, is weighing on shares, with TAP down 4% on Friday.

title: Molson Coors facing sales pressure and increased inflation risks into 2027—Wells Fargo
